Theorem
[Simplex orbifold geometrization] 1. 13.5.3\group tetrahedra Source: thurston:page-0345, thurston:page-0346, thurston:page-0347

Every $n$-orbifold having the combinatorial type of an $n$-simplex admits an elliptic, Euclidean, or hyperbolic structure.
Proof

\sketch Form the matrix whose diagonal entries are $1$ and whose $ij$ entry is $-\cos \alpha _{ij}$, where $\alpha _{ij}$ is the angle between two faces. Every principal submatrix obtained by deleting one row and column is positive definite because it is the Gram matrix of an elliptic vertex link. The full matrix is therefore positive definite, positive semidefinite of rank $n$, or has signature $(n,1)$, and these cases construct respectively the elliptic, Euclidean, and hyperbolic simplex.

□
